name: Nordicism
summary: Nordicism holds that the tall, fair, long-headed peoples of northern Europe form a distinct and superior race whose inherited gifts for leadership and war built Western civilization. Its classic statement, Madison Grant's The Passing of the Great Race (1916), treats race as fixed and rejects equality, democracy and the melting pot. It urges immigration limits by race, laws against mixed marriage and sterilization of those judged unfit, and fears the Nordic stock is being bred out.
scope: The classic American Nordicism of Madison Grant (1916 book, 1921 edition) as described in the scholarship; it excludes Nazi programmes, later race-realist writers and Grant's conservation work. Only Grant's own text and scholarship on it were used, so most statements outside race, heredity, immigration, democracy and eugenics are null.
